claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a formal eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I'm now going to guide you through the assessment. Let me start with the first important question:

**How old is your child (or the oldest child if you have more than one)?**

Please let me know:
- The age of your child/children
- If you have multiple children, I can assess each one

The eligibility rules differ based on whether the child is:
- **Under 16 years old** (generally eligible)
- **16-19 years old** (eligible if in approved education or training)
- **20 years or older** (generally not eligible)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! Alex is 8 years old, so he falls into the "under 16" category, which is great news for eligibility purposes.

Let me continue with the next question:

**Is Alex currently working full-time (30 hours or more per week)?**

This is an important check because even though Alex is under 16, there are specific rules about full-time work that could affect eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8! He's in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That makes sense - Alex is in primary school and not working, which is what we'd expect for an 8-year-old.

Let me continue to the next check in the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me navigate based on Alex's age group:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now we're checking work requirements:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

Since you've already confirmed Alex doesn't work at all (being in primary school), I can proceed with a "yes" answer. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

(For an 8-year-old in primary school, the answer would typically be yes - they wouldn't be receiving these adult benefits - but I want to confirm this with you.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what we'd expect. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

For an 8-year-old in primary school, I'm assuming the answer is no - but I want to confirm. This check is mainly relevant for older children (typically 16+), but I need to ask to be thorough with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8 and in primary school. He's far too young for an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what we'd expect. Let me proceed:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check your residency requirements for Child Benefit. This is an important check for the claimant (that's you).

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the main path for most people
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (with various options like working, seeking work, having sufficient resources, studying, or being a family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** or in certain qualifying countries

Which one of these describes your situation? Or if none of these apply, please let me know your specific circumstances regarding where you live and your immigration status (if relevant).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the straightforward path. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we need to confirm that you are responsible for Alex. Responsibility means either:

1. **You live with the child** - You share a household with them
2. **You contribute to the child's upkeep** - You pay towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.) at least the equivalent amount of Child Benefit
3. **You're paying maintenance** - Under a court order or agreement, you make payments covering the child's upkeep

**Which of these applies to you and Alex?** 

(For most parents living with their child, the first option would apply - you live together.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That confirms you're responsible for Alex. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important point:

**Is anyone else (like Alex's other parent, a grandparent, or anyone else) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or planning to claim for him?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child. The options are:

1. **No one else is claiming** - Just you
2. **Someone else is claiming, but you've agreed who should claim** - You've discussed and agreed
3. **There's a dispute** - You're not sure or there's disagreement about who should claim

Which applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me check Alex's living situation:

**Where does Alex currently live?**

1. **In hospital** - Is Alex currently in hospital?
2. **In care** - Is Alex in local authority care?
3. **Fostered** - Is Alex fostered with another family?
4. **Living normally** - Living at home with you (which seems to be the case based on what you've already told me)

Based on what you've said (Alex lives at home with you in Manchester), I believe the answer is "living normally," but I want to confirm there are no special circumstances.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex is living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or fostered.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now the final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for Alex's housing and upkeep yourself (or with support from family, partner, etc.), without council financial support?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm paying for everything myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! That's the final check completed. Let me proceed to the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! 🎉

## **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!**

### Summary of Your Assessment:

You have met all the eligibility requirements:
- ✅ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- ✅ Alex is not working full-time
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for him
- ✅ No one else is claiming for Alex
- ✅ Alex is living normally at home with you
- ✅ The council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** - You can apply using form CH2 if applying by post
2. **Provide proof of identity** - For both you and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Check the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through tax
5. **Payment schedule** - Child Benefit is paid every 4 weeks (or weekly in certain circumstances)

You can apply online at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's brilliant, thank you so much! That's really helpful. I think I have all the information I need now. I'll get the application sorted out online. Thanks again for your help!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. 😊

You're all set to apply for Child Benefit for Alex online. Just gather the documents you'll need (proof of identity and Alex's birth certificate) and you'll be ready to go.

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit in the future, feel free to come back. Good luck with your application!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Your eligibility has been confirmed and recorded. Best of luck with your application! 👋
